conventions.convention: K_AB has entries k(a_i,b_j), with rows indexed by A and columns by B. Training and test lists have positive finite lengths and may contain repetitions.
Observation noise is centered Gaussian and independent of the process; optional test noise is centered Gaussian and independent of the pair consisting of the process and observation noise.
Ordinary inverse formulas require positive definiteness of the observed covariance K_XX+R. Prior and predictive covariance matrices may be singular; no pseudoinverse extension is asserted.

The conditional formula selects a kernel defined at every observation y; regular conditional versions are determined only almost surely under the observation law. AC is assumed for the Gaussian-process and conditioning interfaces.
The ridge objective uses an unnormalized sum of squared residuals and penalty σ² times the squared norm of g−m, with σ>0. A real Hilbert space with reproducing kernel sections and m∈H is assumed.
Projection is onto a finite-dimensional subspace of a real inner-product space; completeness of the ambient space is unnecessary, and the zero-dimensional subspace is allowed.
Arithmetic counts treat each addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, or square root as one operation; the variance cost is measured after dense factorization.

load_bearing.statement: For a Gaussian process f and independent centered Gaussian observation noise ε with PSD covariance R, define Y=f_X+ε and A_X=K_XX+R. Optional centered Gaussian test noise is independent of the pair (f,ε).

Assume AC and the stated finite GP model with A_X=K_XX+R positive definite. The conditional mean is m_*+K_*X A_X⁻¹(y−m_X), and the conditional covariance is K_**−K_*X A_X⁻¹K_X*, which is PSD and may be singular. Independent Gaussian test noise adds R_* to this covariance. The selected kernel is defined for every y.
For PSD Gram and noise matrices K and R, A=K+R is symmetric PSD. Its ordinary inverse exists if and only if A is positive definite, equivalently if and only if all singular values of A are positive.
Let H be a real inner-product space and V⊆H a finite-dimensional subspace. Each f∈H has a unique p∈V with f−p orthogonal to V, and for every v∈V, ‖f−v‖²=‖f−p‖²+‖p−v‖².

Under AC and the stated real reproducing-Hilbert-space hypotheses with m∈H and σ>0, J(g)=Σ_i(y_i−g(x_i))²+σ²‖g−m‖² has the unique minimizer g_*=m+Σ_i α_i k_xi, where α=(K+σ²I)⁻¹(y−m_X). Its training evaluation vector equals the latent GP conditional-mean vector under independent N_n(0,σ²I) observation noise.
Assume AC and the stated finite GP observation model with A_X positive definite. Then Y has law N_n(m_X,A_X), and log p(y|X,m,k,R)=−(y−m_X)ᵀA_X⁻¹(y−m_X)/2−log det(A_X)/2−n log(2π)/2.

published_dependencies.used_for: Explicit choice assumptions in Gaussian-law construction, canonical GP existence, and conditional-law applications.
Interpretation of process/noise independence and independence from the joint pair.
Scalar-projection characterization, Gaussian affine images, and allowance for singular covariance.
Joint Gaussian finite evaluations, including repeated inputs and degenerate coordinates.
Construction of finite-span orthogonal projection, including the empty basis.
Identification of singular values through the nonnegative square root of A* A.
Orthonormal diagonalization of PSD observed covariance matrices.
Singular-value identification and the finite-dimensional ridge least-squares reduction.
Equivalence between positivity of all singular values and invertibility.
Joint Gaussian stacking of latent evaluations and independent observation noise.
Positive-definite Gaussian density underlying the log marginal likelihood.
Exact finite posterior kernel, PSD Schur complement, all-y version, and independent test-noise addition.
Checking the posterior supplier's probability-kernel argument with singular latent or conditional covariance.
Canonical cylinder-space priors for arbitrary PSD kernels, without sample-path continuity conclusions.
Identification of independent standard-normal finite coordinates in the discontinuity witness.
Limit of decreasing finite-coordinate events in the proof that the equality-kernel GP has no continuous modification.
Dense real Cholesky factorization and triangular-solve operation counts.
Finite-dimensional normal-equation characterization in the ridge minimization proof.
